'''Stallings:''' {{legend0|#7996e2|50–60%}} {{legend0|#6674de|60–70%}} }} {{Elections in Idaho}} The '''1992 United States Senate election in Idaho''' took place on November 3, 1992, alongside other elections to the [[United States Senate]] in other states as well as elections to the [[United States House of Representatives]] and various state and local elections. Incumbent [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] U.S. Senator [[Steve Symms]] decided to retire instead of seeking a third term. Republican nominee and [[Boise]] mayor [[Dirk Kempthorne]] won the open seat, defeating Democratic Congressman [[Richard H. Stallings]]. To date, Stallings' 43 percent is the last time that the Democrats have won more than 40 percent of the vote in a Senate election in Idaho. Instead of seeking re-election in [[1998 United States Senate election in Idaho|1998]], Kempthorne [[1998 Idaho gubernatorial election|successfully ran for governor]]. ==Democratic primary== ===Candidates=== * [[Richard H.
